channel.title: Oath articles
channel.description: Oath product guides and editorial archive

item.title: The Missing Link Between Open Source and the Wallet on Your Phone
item.description: What connects public source code to the app you install? A practical guide to reproducible builds, signed releases, App Store approval, and Oath’s current evidence.

item.title: Your Crypto, Their Permission: The $388 Million Bitget Wake-Up Call
item.description: Bitget’s $388 million breach exposes the difference between a protected balance and control of your money. A sourced examination of exchange failures, self-custody, and the responsibilities that come with your keys.

item.title: Bitcoin Address Types and Recovery Scope in Oath
item.description: Match the address type and imported key scope; changing the visible format does not change the blockchain.

item.title: WalletConnect in Oath: Review the Request, Control the Permission
item.description: Oath now supports WalletConnect. Understand the difference between a session, a signature and an on-chain approval.

item.title: Coldcard’s Weak-Seed Crisis: Complexity Is Not the Same as Security
item.description: The 2026 Coldcard incident did not remotely compromise the devices. It exposed something more fundamental: a sophisticated enclosure cannot protect a seed that was predictable at birth.

item.title: Add a Custom Token Without Trusting Its Name or Symbol
item.description: Add a token by the identity that matters—mainnet plus contract or mint address—then understand what names, symbols, decimals, logos, and prices can and cannot prove.

item.title: Lock Oath Down: Passcode, Biometrics and Auto-Lock
item.description: Choose access controls deliberately and keep a separate recovery method.

item.title: Oath’s Current Security Model: Local Keys and Explicit Network Boundaries
item.description: Understand the protected local vault, password-encrypted backups, and what public network requests reveal.

item.title: Receive Crypto Safely: Match the Network and Address
item.description: Use the address displayed for your selected wallet and exact asset network.

item.title: Why Bitcoin Receiving Addresses Change
item.description: A fresh address can belong to the same supported HD wallet; verify the wallet and network.

item.title: One Wallet, Many Mainnets: How Oath Keeps Accounts and Networks Separate
item.description: One Oath wallet can manage many mainnet identities, but every address, asset, balance, fee, nonce, and transaction remains attached to its exact network.

item.title: Recovery Phrase, Private Key or Encrypted Backup: Choose the Right Import
item.description: Match the recovery format, network and required passphrase to the original wallet.

item.title: Where Crypto Network Fees Actually Go
item.description: A network fee is not one universal charge. Follow it through miner rewards, validator tips, burns, L1 settlement, storage funds, and protocol pools—and see exactly what Oath does with none of it.

item.title: Backup and Restore in Oath: Files, Passwords and Recovery Words
item.description: Choose a recovery method supported by 4.1.3 and verify it before replacing or erasing your phone.

item.title: BIP39 Passphrases and Electrum Seed Extensions in Oath
item.description: A passphrase derives another wallet; it is not an app lock or backup-file password.
